result.title: OrdiHand-GS: Ordinal-Guided Tracking and Hand-Refined Gaussian Avatars for Digital Signers
result.summary: Digital signers, also known as signing avatars, convey sign language through animated virtual humans, where visual fidelity and linguistic intelligibility hinge primarily on the hands. When one hand crosses over the other, two failure modes dominate. First, monocular expressive-human tracking suffers from ordinal depth ambiguity: either hand can satisfy the same 2D landmarks, and the baseline tracker orders wrists at chance level on 365 annotated overlapping frames from How2Sign. Second, hand appearance remains blurred in neural rendering even after geometry is corrected. We propose OrdiHand-GS to address these errors separately. Relative depth from a video depth estimator and apparent hand size vote, with confidence weighting and abstention, for a front-back relation, which enters expressive-human tracking as a hinge on median hand-surface depth. A source-conditioned residual head then refines the local positions of hand-associated UV Gaussians with the avatar backbone and renderer frozen. We instantiate the framework with GUAVA. Against matched unconstrained refinement, wrist-order accuracy rises from 32.9% to 77.3% at a cost of 0.39 pixels of reprojection error, while a random-sign placebo gives no balanced-accuracy gain. A 2x2 factorial evaluation attributes most of the interaction-rendering improvement to tracking-stage refinement, with a smaller additional benefit from the residual.

AI.brief_summary: 针对手语数字人中双手交叠时的前后序深度歧义与手部渲染模糊，提出以视频深度估计与手部表观尺寸做置信加权、可弃权的投票来确定手腕前后关系，并用源条件残差头细化手部相关 UV 高斯，基于 GUAVA 实例化。
AI.relevance_reason: 其置信加权加弃权的多线索裁决机制可能为 LVR 中视觉证据筛选与「STOP」式停止决策提供类比，但该文属 3D 数字人跟踪与渲染，与 latent 推理状态无直接联系，可供核查的线索较远。
